title: Pressure Map Improvements For Garment Fit | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:
The new update to our fitting maps in CLO 2025.0 allows you to directly visualize the pressure exerted by clothing on the avatar for more precise measurements.

Check out other new features here: https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features

Questions? Comment below or ask in our CLO discord server: https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/7814962429977-How-can-I-join-CLO-Discord?utm_campaign=multi_item_banner_JointheOfficialCLODiscord&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=later-linkinbio

transcript: Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe and I'm gonna show you this great update we have with our fitting maps. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn. Okay, so here I've got my avatar with some garments on her and I definitely want to check out this fit. So if I want to check out a fit, there's so many ways in which you can do that, but some of the best things that we have are these fit maps. If you need to find them, they're over in your 3D toggle menu down over here, up over here. And right below the fabric garment like rendering style, there is fit maps. So you have a few different fit map options. You have stress, strain, fit, and pressure. The pressure map's pretty great because you can see the pressure it has onto the avatar. Just make sure you simulate first before you go into the pressure. A pop-up window will come up telling you and reminding you in case you forget, but I remembered, so I just make sure I simulated. I can then turn on my pressure map and what this is doing here is it's telling me where the most amount of pressure is on my avatar. So one that she would probably like feel the garment the most. You can hit hold down control to check the pressure part, which is all right next to your cursor to explain to you and then you can just simply use your right mouse button and click and you're going to see the pressure values here even if you click on areas where like there isn't any pressure you'll see that it's zero even if you click on areas where there isn't even a garment it's gonna say zero so it's always gonna give you some information but now you can click and see exactly how much pressure is happening in on our avatar from our garment now i just want to remind everyone that colors can sometimes be deceiving red isn't always bad blue isn't always good it all depends on the garment that you're fitting so this is an athleisure kind of garment honestly this is looking pretty good and having red over here probably just means that the elastic's working you and that is good so again red isn't always bad blue isn't always good it all depends on the garment that you're fitting and use your own like judgment and yeah thanks so much for watching if you have any questions check out the comment section below and use that somebody will get back to you don't forget to check out the rest of our videos on youtube we've got so many of them and i'll see you in the next one bye bye and like and subscribe while you're at it thanks again so much and keep having fun in chloe
